article_title: DOES FORM-FOCUSED INSTRUCTION AFFECT THE ACQUISITION OF IMPLICIT KNOWLEDGE?
citation: Rod Ellis. (2002). Does Form-Focused Instruction Affect the Acquisition of Implicit Knowledge? A Review of the Research. Studies in Second Language Acquisition, Volume 24, Issue 2. https://doi.org/10.1017/S0272263102002073
title: The role of form-focused instruction in implicit L2 knowledge is a contested theoretical question between peripheral and facilitative/necessary positions
description: The article organizes its review around a theoretical controversy over whether form-focused instruction contributes to second language implicit knowledge. On one side, "Krashen (1993) has argued that the effects of FFI on acquisition are peripheral"; on the other, "N. Ellis (this issue) sees FFI as facilitative and even necessary for developing implicit L2 knowledge." The review of 11 studies of free production is positioned as evidence bearing on this dispute, and its synthesis comes down on the facilitative side.
requirements: Resolving the question requires studies that measure implicit knowledge through learners' free production rather than only controlled or monitored performance
constraints: The review's evidence base is 11 studies of FFI effects on free production, and its conclusions are hedged as what the review "suggests"
target_learning_goals: development of implicit L2 knowledge, particularly grammatical form
examples: The article reviews 11 studies that examined the effect of FFI on learners' free production as the empirical test of the two theoretical positions.
key_sources: Rod Ellis. (2002). Does Form-Focused Instruction Affect the Acquisition of Implicit Knowledge? A Review of the Research. Studies in Second Language Acquisition, Volume 24, Issue 2. https://doi.org/10.1017/S0272263102002073

article_title: Mindfulness and academic performance among nursing students in Saudi Arabia: a cross-sectional study.
citation: Mathkor Darin Mansor. (2025). Mindfulness and academic performance among nursing students in Saudi Arabia: a cross-sectional study. Scientific Reports 15, 27381. https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-025-11911-0
title: Five Facet Mindfulness Questionnaire (FFMQ) as a measure of dispositional mindfulness in nursing students
description: The FFMQ is a 39-item self-report questionnaire with 5-point Likert-type responses ranging from "1" (never or rarely true) to "5" (very often or always true), scoring in the range of 39–195. It measures five subscales: observing, describing, acting with awareness, nonjudging of inner experience, and nonreactivity to inner experience. In this study its internal reliability was α = 0.84 (subscales 0.71–0.87), and it was administered online via Microsoft Forms before mid-semester exams.
requirements: Administration as a self-report instrument; facet scores range between 8 and 40 (nonreactive facet 7 to 35)
constraints: Self-reported measures may be subject to response bias, as the author notes
target_learning_goals: assessment of dispositional mindfulness as a correlate of academic performance
examples: Used with 276 Saudi nursing students, yielding an overall mean mindfulness score of 121.0 (SD = 10.2)
key_sources: Mathkor Darin Mansor. (2025). Mindfulness and academic performance among nursing students in Saudi Arabia: a cross-sectional study. Scientific Reports 15, 27381. https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-025-11911-0
